runs.narrative: I, a mere traveler, stumbled upon a peculiar galley, its very essence suffused with the remnants of salt. The space was tight, with a passage making way to the cold north and a concealed exit heading underground toward the mysterious south. A lone kettle, battered by the sea's harsh elements, lay unresting on the damp floor. With no other company but the echoes of a distant wind and the unsettling quietude of abandonment, I found myself amidst these briny ruins, my destiny unclear, holding only a kettle in my hands—a token from this forsaken voyage.

Amidst the clutter, I discovered a kettle, its metal dented along one side, likely from falls or hard use. Curiosity piqued, I took the kettle, its cold metal surprising against my skin, feeling its weight and the texture of the damage. The galley itself was a relic, silent and abandoned, save for the hiss of the kettle as I briefly gathered it to my hands. A simple, quiet moment in an otherwise deserted place.

There was no sense of grand adventure, just the quiet solitude of exploration in a decaying space, and the gentle clatter of a kettle in my possession, hinting at what obscure purposes it might have served.

Noticing no handle or apparent way to open it, I continued to explore, moving south once more. My exploration thus far has been an intriguing mix of discovery and disappointment, as doors remain locked and hidden passages elusive, leaving me to ponder what further secrets this vessel holds.
